Home
We are one of the UK’s first IB World Schools to offer the full IB curriculum: where we are dedicated to crafting a personalised journey for every student, which we call “igniting the spark of genius in every child.”
Let your little lions explore their exciting new world within the care of our award-winning Early Years team.
The Primary Years Programme in primary school offer a rich and stimulating curriculum designed to generate an enthusiasm for learning and value it as a life-long process.
Our Middle Years and Diploma Programmes in secondary school and sixth form develop life long learners who have the ability to adapt in a rapidly changing society. We instil in our students a sense of belonging in the world around them.
We Outperform Global Benchmarks with Stellar 35-Point IB Average, Equating to 3 As at A Level! ✨
Nurture your child's spark of genius with a Scholarship
We're delighted to announce full wraparound from 7:45 to 5:30 is now included in our fees
Let your little lions explore their exciting new world
2025 World’s Best School Prize for Innovation for Dwight Group School
We are delighted to celebrate the fantastic results of our graduates
Take this opportunity to join our Little Lions Nursery for a chance to meet the other Lions and learn about our caring environment.
Join us at our Woodside Campus for a tour of the school.

pageCache.pageTitle: Scholarships - Current student applicants - Dwight School London | Independent International School
pageCache.text:
The first screening (internal applicants) with a panel made up of our Senior School Leadership will be held in school during the last week of winter term. Successful applicants will move to the second stage of the process.
Second stage will be confirmed closer to the time.
What are the expectations of a scholar?
Scholarship Applications are now open until 20th November 2026.
The deadline for submitting materials (essays, presentations, etc) for the application is midday on 4th January 2027. All online documents (e.g. Google Docs, Word) must be made accessible to all before this deadline.
You can only apply for one scholarship.
Interviews, presentations and auditions will take place on 16th January 2026.
Read the details below and if you require further details then please contact admissions@dwightlondon.org
Scholarship details: Candidates applying for the Alison Cobbin Opening Doors scholarship must demonstrate a potential for academic success as an IB student and contribution to the life of the school. Internal and external applicants are welcome to apply. We will ask you to provide school reports and a teacher reference. All candidates must complete a presentation and an interview.
Eligibility: Open to all students who will enter the Primary Years Programme Year 3 - Year 6.
Award: One scholarship up to 50% remission of school fees for duration of the programme expiring at the end of Year 6.
Application details: Applicants will complete the admissions process which includes parent and student statements as well as school reports. There will also be an external financial assessment.
Brief: Develop a short presentation on a subject that you are passionate about! This could be something you know a lot about or a subject you want to know more about. Students should be prepared to answer a few questions on their presentations, as well as talk about why they want to become a Dwight School student!
Candidates applying for the Science, Technology, Engineering and Mathematics (STEM) scholarship must demonstrate creative thinking and expertise in one of the STEM subjects. We will ask for school reports and a teacher reference. Candidates must also complete a group task/taster day, a presentation and an interview.
Design an Experiment (Candidates will not need to conduct the experiment)
The presentation and report/outline should include the following sections:
Candidates should share their presentation and report/outline with admissions@dwightlondon.org by Midday on 4th Jan 2027
Research and Design a solution to a problem
Choose ONE of the following three briefs:
Create a presentation that uses Design Thinking to explore the problem and present a solution.
The presentation should include the following sections:
Candidates should share their presentation with admissions@dwightlondon.org by Midday on 4th Jan 2027
Applicants are asked to present on one mathematical concept that they find particularly engaging. This presentation should be no longer than 15 minutes and the target audience is a group of non-mathematicians. Students should be prepared to answer questions about their topic at the end. Topics can be a theorem, a practical application, or another mathematical concept.
In addition, applicants will be asked to complete a 45 minute written assessment focusing on general knowledge.
Candidates should share their presentation with admissions@dwightlondon.org by Midday on 4th Jan 2027
Candidates applying for the Arts scholarships must demonstrate an outstanding artistic ability in either Drama, Music or Visual Arts. Candidates will have an interview and an audition.
Middle Years Programme (MYP) Visual Arts Scholarship Criteria Candidates applying for an MYP Visual Arts scholarships would be based upon their ability to demonstrate outstanding artistic ability, technical proficiency in a variety of media, and an emphasis on producing personal and thought provoking artworks.
Visual Arts Application:
Candidates should share their portfolio and sketchbook with Ms Ross by midday on 4th Jan 2027.
Candidates would show how they excel in the practice of art, both inside and beyond the classroom (e.g. through art exhibitions, knowledge of artists, private art lessons and/or extra curricular activities).
Diploma Visual Arts Scholarship Criteria Candidates applying for Diploma Visual Arts scholarships would be based upon their ability to demonstrate outstanding artistic ability, critical and contextual knowledge, technical proficiency in a variety of media, conceptual qualities and an emphasis on producing personal, thought provoking and coherent body of works.
Visual Arts Application:
Candidates should share their portfolio and sketchbook with Ms Ross by midday on 4th Jan 2027.
Candidates would show how they excel in the practice of art, both inside and beyond the classroom (e.g. through art exhibitions, knowledge of artists, work experience, voluntary activities, private art lessons and/or extra curricular activities).
Middle Years Programme (Year 7 - Year 11) and Diploma (Year 12) Theatre Arts Scholarship Brief
Who can apply for a theatre arts scholarship? Any potential candidate can apply for a theatre arts scholarship, as long as they are enthusiastic and committed. We are looking for energy, commitment and potential. At Dwight School we have a very active Theatre department. We also run an extracurricular Film Skool (with an additional fee) - where students devise, produce and edit their own film, taking on a variety of roles such as actor, director, producer, props, costume etc.
Expectations If successful, the drama scholars will be asked to help with all aspects of the extra curriculum drama department, especially when other year groups are producing plays. We would expect them to commit to our film skool programme and rehearse on some weekends.
Candidates should share their monologues and CV with admissions@dwightlondon.org by midday on 4th Jan 2027
Middle Years Programme (MYP) & Diploma Programme (DP) Music Scholarship Criteria
Eligibility & Expectations We welcome applications from students who demonstrate exceptional musical ability, potential, and commitment. While we generally expect a Grade 3 standard for Year 7 entry and a Grade 5 standard for Year 12 entry on their primary instrument, we prioritise a strong musical foundation over rushing through graded exams.
We are looking for musicians who are not only strong performers but also passionate about analysing, discussing, and engaging with music beyond a single style or genre. Successful candidates will demonstrate musical talent, dedication, and diligence in both practice and performance.
Audition Process The audition consists of two rounds:
Round 1 – Video Submission Applicants must submit a video recording of themselves performing two contrasting pieces (different styles/genres) on their primary instrument or voice.
Round 2 – Live Audition Selected applicants will be invited to an in-person audition, where they will perform the same two contrasting pieces live. They will also complete an additional musicianship task, tailored to their instrument:
Composition & Music Technology Applicants Students applying based on compositional work must submit two original pieces before the audition. During the interview, they will be expected to analyse and discuss their creative process, influences, and structural decisions. Scores and digital recordings should be provided where applicable.
Scholar Expectations Music Scholars play a leading role in the Dwight Music Department and are expected to:
Candidates should share a copy of their sheet music, and compositions (if applicable) with admissions@dwightlondon.org by midday on 4th Jan 2027
Candidates applying for a humanities scholarship must demonstrate creative thinking and expertise in English or a humanity based subject (history, geography, politics etc). We will ask for school reports and a teacher reference. Candidates must also complete an essay and an interview.
Candidates are invited to respond critically to their choice of fiction by analysing its key themes. Additionally, candidates should select one of the key themes they have identified in their chosen text, and write their own creative text in the form of poetry or prose.
Candidates should share their choice of fiction, response and a copy of their own creative writing with admissions@dwightlondon.org by Midday on 4th Jan 2027.
Candidates are invited to present a critical analysis on an article/essay/paper on a political, historical or geographical theme of their choice. This will take the form of a short oral interview.
Additionally, candidates will be asked to write an essay. There will be two different questions, one for Years 7-9 (500 words max) and one for Years 10-12 (1000 words max).
During the interview stage, candidates will be asked to present an overview of their essay and answer some questions about it.
Candidates should share a copy of the article/essay/paper for their critical analysis and their essay to admissions@dwightlondon.org by Midday on 4th Jan 2027
Language Acquisition Scholarship (French, Mandarin or Spanish)
Objective The Language Acquisition Scholarship seeks to identify and support students who demonstrate exceptional proficiency, curiosity, and commitment to learning additional languages. We aim to cultivate global citizens who do not merely gain fluency, but who can critically analyse, interpret, and engage with diverse multimodal texts (listening, reading, speaking, and writing) within authentic contexts and produce texts (oral and written) where they demonstrate they can organise ideas clearly and coherently on a variety of personal and global topics.
Eligibility & Expectations We welcome applications from students who demonstrate a high level of linguistic ability and a genuine passion for cultural and linguistic exploration. Current Achievement: Applicants should consistently demonstrate high achievement (an equivalent of a level 7 in the IB or A/A* at A Level) in their Language Acquisition course, including a high level of accuracy and coherence in both spoken and written communication. Expectations will vary according to the length of time the student has been learning the language and the level at which they have studied it. Future Aspirations and motivation: We seek students who intend to pursue advanced language study and who are committed to acting as ambassadors for the language department, supporting peers in developing their linguistic confidence and cultural awareness. For example, leading language-based extracurricular activities (e.g. debate clubs, film discussion groups, assemblies) and actively engaging with the culture of the language studied (through film, current affairs or intercultural discussions). A genuine interest in the subject and commitment are essential. Please note that native speakers will not be considered for their language as a language acquisition scholarship.
Email your submission to admissions@dwightlondon.org by Midday on 4th Jan 2027.
Candidates applying for a sports scholarship must demonstrate a high degree of skill and commitment to a sporting area and/or pursuit. Candidates may be asked to demonstrate this skill level and how they would use it to enrich a sporting team or area of the school. Sporting scholars will participate on a school sports team and/or represent the school at a local, regional or national level. We will ask for school reports and a teacher reference.
There’s some basic criteria you can expect to have to meet for any sports scholarship:
Please write a short presentation about your top sports achievements, your sports goals for the future – including rankings or medals you’re aiming for – and how a scholarship will help you achieve these.
You’ll need to provide a reference or supporting statement from an appropriate individual, such as a National Governing Body (NGB) coach or performance director, team manager, or sports teacher.
Candidates should share their presentation, supporting statement, and any relevant certificates, etc with admissions@dwightlondon.org by Midday on 4th Jan 2027
DWIGHT SCHOOL VISIONARY GRANTs
Grant details: Our Visionary Grants are aimed at supporting local families with an innovative outlook who can contribute to and develop Dwight’s culture of innovation as well as our commitment to preparing students for the future. These grants will offer up to a 50% remission of fees at our world-leading independent international school starting from September 2027. In this context, we refer to all students from Reception to Year 6 in our Junior School and entering Years 7 and 12 in our Senior School.
Deadline: 20th November 2026
Award: There will be a series of grants offering up to a 50% remission of school fees for the duration of the programme commencing from September 2027.
Application details: Families will need to provide a creative pitch or statement illustrating their innovative/visionary outlook and how they might be able to contribute to and develop the Dwight community’s culture of innovation. This should include the fields of work that the family are in as well as any local community connections. They will also need to complete the current admissions process which includes viewing current and past school reports. The application fee will be £200 and a deposit will be £2000 and a taster day for the child/children will be part of the process.
Apply FOR THE GRANT now

pageCache.text:
Franklin School, part of our global network of Dwight Schools in Jersey City, has just been announced as the winner of the 2025 World’s Best School Prize for Innovation by T4 Education.
The significance of this achievement can’t be understated. Head of School, William Campbell, said of his school’s win, “It is more than just an award, it’s proof of what happens when visionary educators and fearless students co-create learning, harness breakthrough tools, and reimagine education itself.”
We are so proud that one of the schools in our network received this recognition — and in only its fourth year. Franklin is also the first school in the US to receive the Prize for Innovation.
The Prize is part of T4’s prestigious World’s Best School Prizes, which honour institutions across the world that are transforming education and changing lives beyond the classroom. You can read more about the win and its significance in this press release.

The ISI is appointed by the Department for Education to inspect all independent schools in England and these inspections are thorough, rigorous and dig deep into the workings of a school.
Dwight was last inspected in May 2025, which found that Dwight School London was deemed to fully meet all areas of the inspection criteria.
The ISI inspectors said that:
“Pupils are well prepared for life in both British and global society.”
“Leaders provide an ambitious age-appropriate curriculum that enriches pupils’ learning. The curriculum and teaching develop pupils’ skills in independent and collaborative learning very well. As a result, pupils develop an enthusiastic and determined approach to their academic work which enables them to make good progress relative to their starting points.”
“Pupils respect each other and appreciate the importance of listening to each other, enabling them to learn about different perspectives to their own.”
“Leaders have established a school community characterised by mutual respect and inclusivity. The school’s global vision of learning is understood by pupils who recognise the importance of listening to and respecting others who have a different social and cultural perspective or background to their own.”

pageCache.pageTitle: Vision & Mission - Dwight School London | Independent International School
pageCache.text:
Dwight School London prepares young people to become leaders in the world. Our students thrive in a curriculum rooted in our three educational pillars. The first is personalised learning; the second, a commitment to community; the third, our global vision.
Personalised programmes extend, challenge and support each student. Our student body comprises a range of academic ability and talent, and we pride ourselves on meeting each student’s needs through the International Baccalaureate Programmes. Based on international standards of excellence, Dwight is committed to realising each student's potential by finding and nurturing their “Spark of Genius”.
Our commitment to the IB ensures each child’s personal development is shaped by the Learner Profile which fosters leadership, initiative and service learning. Students are inspired and educated to make a positive difference to their school, to their communities and to the world. We seek to strengthen the relationships between home and school, and relationships within the school, to maintain an open, welcoming and supportive community.
Our community is made up of a diverse community of students from all over the world. The IB Programmes provide challenges and opportunities that emphasise intercultural awareness while encouraging students to become global thinkers and thus global citizens. Our school extends into other regions of the world through the range of cultures and experiences of our students, and the global network of schools.
Our PhilosophyDwight School London has a commitment to delivering our ethos through every student experience - whether it be academic learning, programmes, or personal activities. We strive for academic excellence and we help to build confident, compassionate young people who influence the future.
Our VisionTo produce students who are inquiring, knowledgeable and caring, while fostering their academic growth. Dwight School London prepares students to move on to further education, to be active, and to be desirable citizens and learners, gaining places at top universities around the world. Our ValuesAs a school our values align very much with the International Baccalaureate’s Learner profile. The traits of Leadership, Curiosity, Thinking & Knowledge, Communication, Integrity, Compassion, Open-mindedness, Balance and Reflection are key to who we are as a school learning community.
The IB Mission StatementThe International Baccalaureate aims to develop inquiring, knowledgeable and caring young people who help to create a better and more peaceful world through intercultural understanding and respect. To this end the organisation works with schools, governments and international organisations to develop challenging programmes of international education and rigorous assessment. These programmes encourage students across the world to become active, compassionate and lifelong learners who understand that other people, with their differences, can also be right.
Diversity, Equality and Inclusion
Our goal is to ensure that our school is fully inclusive in meeting the needs of all children. We recognise that children and their families come from diverse backgrounds, and that all families have needs and values that arise from their socio-economic, ethnic, cultural and/or religious backgrounds. Children grow up in diverse family structures that include - but are not limited to - two-parent, single-parent and same-sex parents. While some children have close links with extended families of grandparents, aunts, uncles and cousins, others may be more removed from close kin, or may live with other relatives or foster carers.Our statement
At Dwight, we understand that our School’s community is enriched by its members’ varying backgrounds. We seek to raise awareness of all protected characteristics:
- Age - Disabilities - Gender reassignment - Marriage & civil partnerships - Pregnancy & maternity - Race - Religion or belief - Sex - Sexual orientation
At Dwight School London, no single member of our community is the same. Our differences are what makes us strong. We draw on our diversity of thought, experience and vision to build a safe space for all to learn, grow and thrive. In order to ignite the spark of genius in every child, our mission is to ensure everyone feels included.

pageCache.pageTitle: Arts - Dwight School London | Independent International School
pageCache.text:
The arts are integral to a Dwight education and we offer students a great variety of activities in which to create, express themselves, find their sparks of genius and flourish.
At Dwight School London, we believe every child has the potential to learn and appreciate music. Our goal extends beyond teaching students how to perform; we aim to foster lifelong music enthusiasts.
Our music courses encompass the study of music from various countries and regions, exploring diverse cultures and historical influences. Students also engage in learning different instruments, collaborating with others, and mastering music theory and composition using online software.
We offer a rich array of musical activities at Dwight School London. Our students have the opportunity to perform in at least two global concerts each year, including prestigious events like the London Choir Festival and the Global Concert. They have also had the honour of performing at renowned venues such as Carnegie Hall and Lincoln Center in New York.
Our music programme includes a broad range of activities, from ensembles like choirs, rock bands, chamber orchestras, and jazz bands.
Junior and senior students enhance their talents, skills, and knowledge through the Conservatory programme, which offers individual lessons and ensemble instruction during school hours and on Saturdays.
The Dwight School London Music Conservatory Programme provides students with the opportunity to take individual music lessons and ensemble coaching in order to develop their musical talents, skills and knowledge.
Students are taught by teachers from prestigious institutions such as The Royal College of Music, The Royal Conservatoire of Scotland, The Guildhall School of Music & Drama and The Royal Welsh College of Music & Drama, as well as musicians performing in well established jazz ensembles, orchestras, choirs and rock bands.
The London Academy for Music and Dramatic Arts is the oldest specialist Drama school in The British Isles. Their internationally recognised 8 grade system in performance is in line with the graded music tuition from Trinity, ABRSM & RSL.
The Verse & Prose and Acting Syllabi builds confidence, and improves communication and listening skills.
Solo Acting in upper school involves the study and performance of dramatic monologues. Verse and Prose syllabus in lower school, offers a grounding in pronunciation, diction, breathing through poems and prose.
LAMDA lessons are 30 minutes long with a rotating timetable so that pupils can maintain their studies in core subjects. It is worth noting that LAMDA Grades 6, 7 and 8 offer UCAS Points. Essential to support your child’s University application at a time when competition is at an all time high.
The standard of LAMDA at Dwight is extremely high, with 99% of all Dwight pupils achieving Merit or Distinction in their graded exams. To find out more or to book your child’s free taster session follow this link. Complete the form below by adding LAMDA as your child’s chosen instrument.
Students are encouraged to discover their own unique view of the world and the skills to express it. They explore the full range of media, including architectural drawing, collage, drawing, painting, multimedia, photography, printmaking, sculpture, installations and film making. Through gallery visits, students learn and experience art as consumers. Our art room is fully resourced with the latest equipment and technology, where pupils are sure to find their artistic inspiration.
Students learn about theatre arts both on and behind the stage, developing a wide range of creative and technical skills. They play a significant role in writing, producing, staging and performing productions ranging from Shakespeare, Commedia dell’Arte and interpretations of Chekov to Broadway musicals, mysteries and much more.
Students with a passion for film can join our Film School weekly workshops to develop their film scripts and shoot their short films with industry-standard equipment. They learn how to light scenes, frame shots, record sound, direct and edit. They have the privilege of seeing their final cuts premiere on the big screen at The Curzon Cinema in central London.
